# receipt.computer

> A public, login-free verifier for Motebit receipts. Paste any signed Motebit artifact — an execution receipt, a tool-invocation receipt, a content manifest — and read its verdict: signature validity and the identity-binding rung (integrity-only, key commitment, pinned, anchored), plus revocation.

receipt.computer is the consumer side of Motebit's self-attesting system: every claim the protocol makes is user-verifiable, offline-first, with no account and no install. Verification is pure — canonical JSON → SHA-256 → Ed25519 — and external anchoring (Solana) is additive evidence, never a gatekeeper.

## What the rungs mean

- **integrity-only**: the signature verifies against the key embedded in the artifact — the artifact is internally consistent, but the key→identity binding is unproven.
- **canonical form**: every identity-bearing field the signer writes must be in exact canonical form to earn anything above integrity-only: the motebit id (below), `public_key` exactly 64 lowercase hex characters, `signature` exactly unpadded base64url of 64 bytes, and `suite` exactly `motebit-jcs-ed25519-b64-v1`. The key and signature decode leniently, so a re-spelled field (an appended character, whitespace, a sign, upper case, padding) can still verify; such a receipt reads integrity-only with revocation "not established", and the page says the field is "not in canonical form" (or "suite not recognized") — never that it is forged. The page's own revocation scan uses the decoded key, so a memo for the key is reported however the receipt spells it.
- **key commitment**: the motebit id is the self-certifying commitment to the signing key (its original key) — a UUIDv8 derived from the key, or a did:key that encodes it — and no identity chain the page checked binds that key at the time the receipt claims — either none was checked, or the one the relay served does not (the page says which). Not shown as a bound identity.
- **pinned**: the page's own check finds the key inside the time window of the identity chain the relay serves for that motebit id, at the time the receipt claims. That time is the receipt's `completed_at`, which the signer writes, so pinned does not prove when the receipt was issued: a key retired later can still sign a receipt dated inside its old window. For a self-certifying id, the chain must root at the key the id commits to. Only an exactly canonical id binds at all: a lowercase UUIDv8 or did:key, or a lowercase legacy UUIDv7/v4. Any other form, such as one with invisible or look-alike characters, whitespace, upper case or a prefix, binds no key, and the page says the id is not in canonical form. A guardian-recovery link is not honoured, because the only source of its guardian key is the relay's own record. The window is only as complete as the chain served: a later rotation the relay did not serve would not show.
- **anchored**: the identity log's Merkle root is found on-chain (Solana) at the relay's pinned address through an RPC the operator does not run. The public page reads Solana through Motebit's RPC proxy, and labels those reads "via Motebit's RPC proxy (not independently confirmed)". It never shows them as anchored or as a revocation ✓.
- **revocation**: shown as checked only after a complete scan of the anchor address the relay declares (in its transparency declaration), through an independent RPC, finds no memo naming the key; that is the scope of the check, not the whole chain. A failed, truncated or proxy-only scan reads "not established". Any revocation memo found for the key is shown as "REVOCATION REPORTED (unauthenticated)" with where it was read, whatever its date relative to the receipt's `completed_at`: that time is the signer's own claim, so a memo dated after it clears nothing. A memo naming the key with no usable date is reported too. The page does not check who posted the memo, so it fails closed without claiming the key was revoked.

## Use it

- [receipt.computer](https://receipt.computer): paste a receipt, get the verdict.
- [Verification spec and docs](https://docs.motebit.com): the protocol behind the verdicts.
- [`@motebit/verifier` on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@motebit/verifier): the same verification as a library — consume it, never fork it.
- [motebit.com](https://motebit.com): the sovereign agent runtime that mints these receipts.
